Metadata.title: WWF Crotone — Volunteer Camps 2026
Metadata.description: Join the WWF Crotone volunteer camps: protect Caretta caretta sea turtles, clean up beaches, rescue wildlife. Summer 2026, San Leonardo di Cutro (KR), Calabria.

Home.heroSubtitle: Join the WWF Crotone volunteer camps. We monitor Caretta caretta nests, clean the beaches of the Capo Rizzuto MPA and rescue wildlife. Sunday-to-Sunday weeks, June to September.
Home.activitiesSubtitle: Each week combines hands-on conservation, training and discovery of the Calabrian territory.
Home.turnsSubtitle: Sunday to Sunday, June 21 to September 13, 2026. Choose your week.
Home.storyTitle: A story of legality and environment
Home.storyBody: You'll stay at the C.E.L.A., a property confiscated from organised crime and returned to the community. The camp protects the Crotone province: the Capo Rizzuto Marine Protected Area, the Vergari Reserve, the San Leonardo di Cutro SCI.
Home.finalCtaBody: Limited spots per turn. Book your week of conservation, training and community.

About.title: About us
About.intro: WWF Crotone is the local section of WWF Italia ETS, active in the Crotone province for biodiversity conservation, sea turtle protection and environmental education.
About.wwfCrotoneBody: The local section operates in the Crotone territory with conservation projects, summer volunteer camps, environmental education and awareness campaigns. It collaborates with institutions, schools and other third-sector organisations.
About.tartamarBody: TARTAMar Calabria is WWF Italia's regional project to monitor and protect the nesting sites of the Caretta caretta sea turtle along the Calabrian coast. Calabria is the second Italian region by number of nests, just behind Sicily. The project involves constant beach monitoring, search for nesting tracks, securing nests and data collection, using drones and Totò, our turtle dog (specialised canine unit) to locate nests.
About.crasTitle: Collaboration with the CRAS of Catanzaro
About.crasBody: WWF Crotone works with the C.R.A.S. (Wild Animal Recovery Center) of Catanzaro for the recovery, stabilisation and rehabilitation of wildlife in difficulty. Volunteers provide operational support during first-aid activities.
About.celaTitle: The C.E.L.A. — Center for Education on Legality and the Environment
About.celaBody: Volunteers stay at the C.E.L.A., a property confiscated from the mafia in San Leonardo di Cutro and granted on loan to WWF Crotone. The facility has a kitchen, common room, outdoor dining area, garden and dormitory rooms with bunk beds and shared bathroom. The beach is about 200 metres away. The C.E.L.A. is a concrete symbol of legality and rebirth: a property returned to the community, now a place of education, sharing and respect for the environment.
About.vergariBody: One of the natural jewels of the Crotone territory is the Vergari Regional Nature Reserve, destination of a guided excursion during the camp.

Activities.title: Camp activities
Activities.intro: Each week combines core conservation activities, secondary cultural activities and training moments.
mainList: Search for Caretta caretta nests, protection and support during hatching
Aquarium maintenance and management of the Capo Rizzuto Marine Turtle Recovery Center (CRTM)
Cleanup of beaches of particular naturalistic interest in the Capo Rizzuto MPA
Recovery and first aid of wildlife in collaboration with the CRAS of Catanzaro
Lesson on organised crime, legality and environment
Activities.secondaryIntro: Cultural and excursion activities take place compatibly with the camp's operational needs and the progress of the core activities.
secondaryList: Excursion to the Vergari Regional Nature Reserve (KR)
Visit to the Capocolonna Archaeological Park and Museum (extra booking)
Visit to Le Castella (Capo Rizzuto island), with optional extra visit to the Aragonese Castle of Le Castella
Environmental education on the beaches of the MPA (Marine Protected Area)
Activities.monitoringBody: Territory monitoring is carried out daily together with WWF operators, in the early hours of the morning. Turtle emergence tracks are intercepted before bathers arrive: human footsteps quickly erase the marks in the sand. Identified nests are monitored over time, until hatching, with possible night surveillance to ensure their protection. Alongside the operators works Totò, our turtle dog (canine unit) trained to search for Caretta caretta nests.
Activities.tartamarBody: TARTAMar Calabria is WWF Italia's regional project to monitor and protect the nesting sites of the Caretta caretta sea turtle along the Calabrian coast. Calabria is the second Italian region by number of nests, just behind Sicily. The project involves constant beach monitoring, search for nesting tracks, securing nests and data collection, using drones and Totò, our turtle dog (specialised canine unit) to locate nests.

Dates.title: Dates & Booking
Dates.intro: Volunteer camps run Sunday to Sunday. Choose one or more turns from the 12 available, June 21 to September 13, 2026.
Dates.costBody: The fee is €430 per person per turn (€400 for WWF members). Minors pay an additional €20 for insurance. Discounts for groups of at least 5 people. If you register for multiple consecutive turns, the fee is calculated per week.
Dates.multiTurnInfo: You can register for multiple consecutive turns. The total fee will be calculated automatically based on the number of weeks selected.
Dates.depositBody: The registration fee of €100 (deducted from the total) must be paid by bank transfer to WWF Provincia di Crotone.
Dates.causaleValue: Registration of: First and last name, chosen camp number
includedList: Meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner (menus for vegetarians, vegans and celiacs)
Accommodation in dormitory rooms with bunk beds, en-suite bathroom with hot water and air conditioning
Donation to the national WWF campaign
Excursions, museum entries and guided tours

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.intro: Everything you need to know before signing up for the WWF Crotone volunteer camps.

items.q: Can I join if I'm not a WWF member?
items.a: Yes. The fee is €430 for non-members, €400 for WWF members. The WWF membership card is included in the participation fee.

items.q: Can I join if I'm a minor?
items.a: Yes, minors can join with the consent of a parent or guardian and with a €20 surcharge for insurance. The consent form must be signed by the parent/guardian.
Sleeping bag or sheets, towels, swimsuit, comfortable shoes, hat, sunscreen, water bottle, torch for night shifts, repellent and comfortable clothes. A light jacket for the evening.
At the C.E.L.A. in shared rooms of up to 8 people with bunk beds and shared bathroom, air conditioning and hot water.
Yes: breakfast, lunch and dinner. Volunteers self-manage the kitchen with the help of the coordinators. Menus are available for vegetarians, vegans and celiacs.
Core activities are adapted to the weather. In case of bad weather, indoor training and Aquarium/CRTM maintenance activities are carried out.

items.q: How do I get to Crotone?
items.a: By plane: Crotone-Sant'Anna airport or Lamezia Terme. By train: Crotone or Botricello stations. By bus: Crotone bus station or Piazzale Nettuno. WWF Crotone offers a transfer service to/from the camp (€10 surcharge per leg from Lamezia). Arrivals and departures in the middle of the day are recommended.
Yes, the C.E.L.A. has Wi-Fi available for volunteers.

items.q: Can I come with my family?
items.a: Yes, the camp is open to families. Groups of at least 5 people get a discount.

Yes, at the end of the camp a certificate of participation is issued, valid as university training credits or as PCTO for secondary schools. We recommend contacting universities and schools for agreements or protocols.
By bank transfer to WWF Provincia di Crotone, IBAN IT30V0306909606100000107334. The €100 registration fee secures your spot; the balance is due one week before the camp starts.

items.q: Is there a cap on spots per turn?
items.a: Yes, each turn has a maximum capacity of 20 volunteers. We recommend booking early to secure your spot.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.intro: Information notice pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and Italian Legislative Decree 196/2003 as amended.

sections.p: WWF Crotone — Local section of WWF Italia ETS. Email: wwfcrotone26@gmail.com. Phone: +39 351 3945109.

The site collects data voluntarily entered by the user in the volunteer camp registration form: name, surname, date of birth, email, phone, health and dietary data necessary for camp organisation, parent/guardian data for minors, choice of turn. For the newsletter it collects only the email address.

Data is processed to: manage camp registrations, organise logistics and healthcare on site, issue participation certificates, respond to information requests, send camp communications (with explicit consent). Health data is processed only to ensure the safety of the participant during the camp.

Processing is based on the performance of a contract (camp registration), the explicit consent of the data subject (for health data, marketing communications and image use), and the fulfilment of legal obligations.

Registration data is kept for the time necessary to organise the camp and for the following 10 years for regulatory and insurance obligations, unless early deletion is requested. Newsletter data is kept until unsubscription.
Data is accessible to WWF Crotone camp managers and, for health purposes, to first-aid staff. It is not transferred to third parties, except by legal obligation.

You have the right to access your data, rectify it, erase it, restrict processing, object and withdraw consent. To exercise your rights write to wwfcrotone26@gmail.com. You have the right to lodge a complaint with the Italian Data Protection Authority (www.garanteprivacy.it).
